_strings.@@0cf72415eb0e: Credit for Taxes Paid to Other States — Kansas residents whose Kansas adjusted gross income (KAGI, line 3 of K-40) includes income earned in another state and who were required to pay income tax to that other state on that income. 'State' includes the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, U.S. territories/possessions, and foreign countries (foreign taxes run through the Worksheet for Foreign Tax Credit first, and no credit is allowed if the foreign tax was claimed as a federal itemized deduction).

_strings.@@a7da78c30e3e: Treaty conformity — KS conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from KS income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the KS return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Kansas Form K-40 starts from federal adjusted gross income (K-40 Line 1, "Federal adjusted gross income (as reported on your federal income tax return)"), and Kansas modifications are made only on Schedule S Part A. The 2025 Schedule S Part A "Additions to Federal Adjusted Gross Income" remains an enumerated, closed list: state/municipal bond interest, KPERS contributions, Kansas expensing recapture (K-120EX), charitable contributions used for the Low Income Student Scholarship credit, IRC 163(j) business interest expense carryforward, unqualified First-Time Home Buyer savings account withdrawals, and "other additions" (federal income tax refunds, partnership/S-corp/fiduciary adjustments, community service contribution credit add-back, LQESP nonqualified withdrawals, energy-credit amortization, nonresident ad valorem taxes). There is NO add-back for federally tax-treaty-exempt income anywhere in Part A. Because income exempt under a U.S. tax treaty is already excluded from federal AGI and Kansas has no add-back, it flows through and is not re-taxed by Kansas -> conforms. (Source: 2025 Individual Income Tax Booklet, ip25.pdf, K-40 Line 1 and the Schedule S Part A line-by-line instructions; 2025 Schedule S, schs25.pdf.)

_strings.@@bf4cbc914238: Homestead Refund (property tax / circuit-breaker relief) — Kansas resident residing in Kansas the ENTIRE year of 2025 who owned and occupied a Kansas home, AND is over 55 years old, or is blind or disabled, or has a dependent child under 18 who lived with them all year. Related claims: Form K-40PT property tax refund (homeowners at least 65 years old, household income $25,380 or less — refund is 75% of property taxes paid) and Form K-40SVR (seniors at least 65, disabled veterans, and spouses of veterans 65 or older, household income not more than $58,041). A claimant who receives the K-40PT refund cannot also claim a Homestead refund.

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: 2025 Form K-40, Line 8: 'Tax (from Tax Tables or Tax Computation Schedule)'. Instructions: 'LINE 8 (Tax): If line 7 is $100,000 or less, use the Tax Tables beginning on page 27 to find the amount of your tax. If line 7 is more than $100,000, you will need to use the Tax Computation Worksheet on page 34 to compute your tax.' Line 7 = Line 3 (KAGI) minus Line 6 (Line 4 standard/itemized deduction + Line 5 exemption allowance); 'if less than zero, enter 0'. Verified exemption kinds shipped but NOT applied by this op (compute them on the form): disabled_veteran ($2,320 — Disabled Veteran Personal Exemption: an additional $2,320 per honorably discharged veteran certified by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs as receiving disability compensation at the 100% rate (permanent, service-sustained), 'for tax year 2025 and all tax years thereafter' — RAISED from 2024's $2,250. Printed on the 2025 K-40 front as an 'X $2,320 =' box ('enter the total number of disabled veterans being claimed including yourself'). NOT applied by calc.state_tax; claim it on the form and it flows into Line 5 (or, since the amount now equals the per-dependent $2,320, capture it through dependents_count).) This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: 2025 IS A NO-CHANGE YEAR FOR THE RATE SCHEDULE, STANDARD DEDUCTION, AND ALLOWANCE: the 2024 SB 1 restructure carries forward exactly — two brackets, 5.2% on taxable income up to $23,000 ($46,000 married filing joint) and 5.58% above; standard deductions $3,605/$8,240/$6,180/$4,120 (single/MFJ/HoH/MFS); exemption allowance $18,320 (MFJ) or $9,160 (all other statuses) plus $2,320 per dependent and $2,320 additional for Head of Household. Filing thresholds are unchanged too. Verified against BOTH the 2025 booklet worksheet and the independent 2025 K-40ES schedules — no 2025-session rate change appears in either. Base guidance: Supply K-40 Line 3, Kansas adjusted gross income (KAGI) = Line 1 federal AGI ('as reported on your federal income tax return') plus or minus Line 2 net modifications from Schedule S Part A. Most filers have no Kansas modifications, in which case Line 3 equals federal AGI. The op then subtracts the shipped standard deduction (K-40 Line 4) and the exemption allowance (Line 5) to reach Line 7 taxable income, to which the two-bracket schedule applies. EXEMPTION COUNT CONVENTION (unchanged for 2025): pass exemptions_count=1 for single/MFS filers and 2 for married filing jointly — the $9,160-per-count math reproduces the form's $9,160/$18,320 filing-status allowance exactly. Pass dependents_count = number of federal dependents (each $2,320; never count yourself or your spouse). HEAD OF HOUSEHOLD: pass exemptions_count=1 AND add 1 to dependents_count — the form grants HoH an additional $2,320 exemption ('If your filing status is Head of Household, you are allowed an additional exemption of $2,320'), which equals the per-dependent amount. Example: HoH with 1 dependent -> exemptions_count=1, dependents_count=2 (= $9,160 + $4,640). Missing it understates the exemption by $2,320. (For 2025 there is no longer a food sales tax credit, so the 2024 caveat that the HoH extra did not count toward that credit no longer applies.) QUALIFYING SURVIVING SPOUSE maps to HEAD OF HOUSEHOLD in Kansas, not MFJ: the 2025 booklet Filing Status instruction says 'If your federal filing status is Qualifying Widow(er) with Dependent Child, check the Head of Household box.' Do not use a QSS->married_filing_jointly mapping for Kansas — compute QSS filers as head_of_household (single-status brackets, $6,180 standard deduction, $9,160 allowance + the extra $2,320 via dependents_count). Tax-table mandate below $100,000: K-40 Line 8 REQUIRES the Tax Tables when Line 7 taxable income is $100,000 or less; the Tax Computation Worksheet is used only above $100,000. The 2025 table uses $50-wide bands computed at band midpoints, so bracket math may differ by a dollar or two within a table band — the filed form must use the table. The table's first row is '$26 - $50 -> $2' in both columns. NO zero-tax cliff (since 2024): the 2025 Kansas Tax Table starts at '$26 - $50 -> $2' and the Tax Computation Worksheet brackets start at $0 — marginal bracket math applies from the first dollar of taxable income. Rounded worksheet constants (re-derived for 2025, unchanged): the Tax Computation Worksheet computes tax as 5.58% x the ENTIRE taxable income minus a subtraction amount. The exact continuity constants are $87.40 (Single/HoH/MFS: 5.58% x 23,000 - 5.2% x 23,000 = 1,283.40 - 1,196.00) and $174.80 (MFJ, at $46,000); the printed constants are $87 and $175. So above the breakpoint the filed worksheet result can be up to $0.40 HIGHER (Single/HoH/MFS) or $0.20 LOWER (MFJ) than exact marginal bracket math — up to $1 difference after whole-dollar rounding. The 2025 K-40ES schedules state the same brackets with EXACT constants ($1,196 / $2,392 plus 5.58% of the excess), which is what this op's marginal math reproduces. One rate schedule covers Single, Head of Household, and Married Filing Separate ($23,000 breakpoint — both the booklet worksheet and the K-40ES print a single combined schedule for all three); it is duplicated per status here. Married Filing Joint has its own schedule with the breakpoint at exactly twice that ($46,000). Standard deduction for people 65 or older and/or blind is NOT modeled: the 2025 booklet worksheet replaces the base amounts with $4,455/$5,305 (Single, 1/2 boxes), $8,940/$9,640/$10,340/$11,040 (MFJ, 1-4 boxes), $4,820/$5,520/$6,220/$6,920 (MFS, 1-4 boxes), $7,030/$7,880 (HOH, 1/2 boxes) — i.e., +$850 per checked box for Single/HOH and +$700 per box for MFJ/MFS (all unchanged from 2024). Compute K-40 Line 4 from that worksheet in those cases. Kansas itemized deductions (Kansas Schedule A, K-40 Line 4) may be claimed instead of the standard deduction even if the federal return did not itemize — itemizers are not modeled; MFS spouses must both use the same method (if one itemizes, both must). NEW 2025 ADDITIONAL EXEMPTIONS, NOT MODELED by the personal/dependent keys: $2,320 for each dependent child BORN in the tax year, and $2,320 for the parent(s) of a child who is STILLBORN during the tax year (2025 booklet, Additional Exemptions - Dependent Children / Stillborn Births; three 'X $2,320' boxes print on the 2025 K-40 front). Each is claimed on the form and flows into Line 5. If you want them reflected through this op, add one to dependents_count per qualifying exemption — the amount is identical ($2,320). Disabled Veteran Personal Exemption is shipped as verified DATA only and is NOT applied by calc.state_tax: an additional $2,320 per honorably discharged veteran certified by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs as receiving disability compensation at the 100% rate (permanent, service-sustained), 'for tax year 2025 and all tax years thereafter' — RAISED from 2024's $2,250. Claim it on the K-40 front ('enter the total number of disabled veterans being claimed including yourself'); it flows into Line 5. Because its amount now equals the per-dependent $2,320, it can alternatively be captured through dependents_count. Claimed as a dependent by another taxpayer: the 2025 instructions zero only the DEPENDENTS box ('enter "0" in the number of dependents box'); like 2024 they print no rule zeroing the filing-status allowance itself. Confirm the dependent-filer treatment at the DOR before relying on the $9,160 allowance for such a filer (see the pack's unverified list). THE FOOD SALES TAX CREDIT NO LONGER EXISTS FOR 2025 — do not carry 2024's $125-per-qualified-exemption credit forward. The 2025 booklet has no food-sales-tax-credit section and the 2025 K-40 front has no lines A-H block; K-40 line 17 is now the EITC and line 18 is the Total tax balance (in 2024, line 18 was the food sales credit and line 19 the balance), and the refundable EITC portion moved from line 23 to line 22. CREDITS are not modeled by this op (they subtract from tax, not from income): the Kansas EITC is 17% of the federal EITC (Line 17 nonrefundable use, Line 22 refundable remainder); the credit for child and dependent care expenses is 50% of the federal Form 2441 credit (Line 14); the credit for taxes paid to other states is the worksheet's lesser-of amount (Line 13); certificate credits (Apprenticeship K-24, Affordable Housing K-25, and the rest of the Line 15 list) are claimed on Line 15. Kansas tax on lump sum distributions is not modeled: residents add 13% of the federal Form 4972 tax on K-40 Line 11. Nonresidents and part-year residents are not modeled: they compute the full-year tax on Line 8, then multiply by the Schedule S line B23 nonresident allocation percentage (K-40 Lines 9-10) to get nonresident tax. All K-40 money entries are whole dollars; the engine's round-half-up to whole dollars matches the form's presentation.
